items.b: GOLD $4,366.10, SILVER $64.44, PLATINUM $1,753.00: THE BOARD RETURNS TO 19 AUGUST
items.t: All four metals fell in Tuesday's early session and all four were written back to the tape at press time. Against this tape's 19 August marks gold is 0.14% higher, silver 2.09% and platinum 1.56%. Thirteen days of trading have been handed back. Gold is 5.98% below its 24 August high of $4,643.90.

items.b: SILVER IS FURTHEST FROM ITS HIGH AND GOLD IS NEAREST
items.t: Silver sits 8.43% below $70.37 struck 28 August, palladium 7.19% below $1,405.00, platinum 6.90% below $1,883.00 and gold 5.98% below $4,643.90. The gold-silver ratio widened to 67.75 from 66.46. That is the order the board takes when the trade sells the whole complex rather than a view on one metal.

items.b: THE ONE-CARAT LAB-GROWN REFERENCE DROPS $13 IN A SESSION, TO $687
items.t: CaratRadar's one-carat average fell 1.8571% on 1 September, from $700. Every other move on this tape since 5 August was three dollars or less, the largest being $3 on 14 August. The reference has lost $24, or 3.3755%, since its 8 August high of $711.

items.b: CHOW TAI SENG'S REVENUE FELL 20.79% AND ITS GROSS MARGIN ROSE 6.61 POINTS
items.t: Half-year revenue RMB 3.641 billion, net profit RMB 450 million (down 24.24%), gross margin 36.95% against 30.34%. Second-quarter profit fell 54.2%, more than twice the six-month rate. The company blames swings in the gold price for pressuring jewellery consumption.

items.b: THE SAME SIX MONTHS CUT TWO CHINESE JEWELLERS IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS
items.t: Chow Sang Sang's half to 30 June, reported here 29 August, took HK$12.88 billion of revenue (up 17%) and HK$2.15 billion of profit (up 139%). Chow Tai Seng's revenue fell a fifth over the identical window. One was long the metal on its balance sheet, the other selling it across a counter.

items.b: CORRECTION: THE MUSEE LALIQUE LOSS IS 4.5 MILLION EUROS, NOT 4 MILLION
items.t: Yesterday's Vienna necklace piece reached back to the first estimate of 7 July, about 20 pieces at 4 million euros. The completed inventory published the next day put 27 pieces at 4.5 million euros, about $5.1 million. This paper's own report of 14 July carried the revised figure and was correct as published. The Louvre figure of $102 million is now sourced to the Paris prosecutor, 21 October 2025.

tape_ts: 1 Sep 2026 - Kitco, re-read by the Editor at press time and written back to the tape under the One-Price Rule. A metals story leads, so all four were re-read and all four had moved off the 05:00 mark: gold $4,366.10 (down $82.186, 1.8476%), silver $64.44 (down $2.0802, 3.1272%), platinum $1,753.00 (down $37.9185, 2.1173%) and palladium $1,304.00 (down $52.114, 3.8429%), each against Monday's close. Checked mid-to-mid against CNBC rather than bid-to-last, so a wide spread cannot manufacture a divergence: gold 0.0337%, silver 0.1033%, platinum 0.0142%, palladium 0.1499%. All four inside the band on both pages, so no outside-source divergence is disclosed this session. Palladium's quoted spread was $40.00, 3.067% of the bid, with CNBC's last sitting on its midpoint.
